BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 Theorem 5.17 establishes proper blocked structural identifiability but does not give a singleton-allowing endpoint-family separator.
BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 Question 5.19 leaves graphical edge-colored model equivalence open; Chickering1995 covers only uncolored DAG reversals.

soundness_flags.one_line: For arbitrary positive-definite sample covariance, g_E invokes L_E(Σ) as a block-equal structural matrix but only says “parent regressions”; ordinary parent regression need not obey E's coefficient blocks, so the plug-in effect map and its derivatives are ambiguous off-model.

source_verification_receipts.version: JRSSB 88(3), 2026, primary journal version; theorem numbering differs from arXiv v3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The journal paper studies BPEC-DAGs and establishes their structural identifiability; arXiv v3 presents the corresponding result as Theorem 5.17.

A BPEC-DAG is blocked and properly edge-colored, hence has no color class of size below two; Theorem 5.17 gives structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs and Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-colored model equivalence.
For Markov-equivalent DAGs, Theorem 2 gives a sequence of distinct covered reversals, one per disagreeing arrow, preserving equivalence after each reversal.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory 4, 2023, pp. 639–650, primary publication
source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 4.1; theorem text corroborated in arXiv:2308.08959 pp. 9–10
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a fixed partition of vertices sharing innovation variances, model equivalence holds exactly when DAGs have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders and the same parent sets at vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
The paper gives a linear-time-delay algorithm for enumerating ordinary MEC DAGs and extends enumeration to background-knowledge representations.
IDA combines estimation of an ordinary equivalence class with intervention-effect calculations and proves consistent estimation of distinct possible-effect values.
The paper treats selection among finitely many smoothly curved exponential-family models with dimension penalties and establishes consistency of its model-choice criterion.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define L_E(Σ) off-model explicitly via target-local block-constrained least squares (including the block-sum Gram map), then state its rationality and derivative domain before using g_E(S_n).
Add a worked four- or five-node mixed singleton/repeated-block example that computes the static signature, its complete reversal component, and two distinct member-labelled total-effect maps.

State a separate finite-model selection lemma that rules out strict containment by lower-dimensional nonequivalent blocked models, making the algebraic exceptional-set argument independently auditable before claiming BIC component recovery.

recommended_next_step: Revise the off-model definition of the block-constrained effect functional and its delta-method map, then advance the complete singleton-allowing equivalence theorem as the field-tier kernel.
